newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian harvest so far 63 mln T bunker, pace slows.
newsitem.headline: Russian harvest so far 63 mln T bunker, pace slows.

text.p: Russia has so far harvested about 63 million tonnes bunker weight of grains, but the pace of harvesting will be very slow this week, Interfax news agency quoted an agriculture ministry official as saying on Thursday.
Ivan Gridasov, head of the ministry's crops-growing section, was quoted as saying Russia's net harvest this year would likely be 10 million tonnes above last year's official 63.4 million tonnes.
First Deputy Agriculture Minister Vladimir Shcherbak, quoted by Interfax, gave the same estimate earlier this week, which is below official government forecasts of 75-77 million tonnes.
Gridasov said cold weather, rain and a lack of fuel and tractor spare parts meant that only two million ha sown to grains would be harvested this week, half the four million harvested last week.
Average yields were 1.66 tonnes per ha, above last year's 1.46 tonnes.
Crops over 3.5 million ha had been lost, Gridasov said, but he did not specify which crops.
He said that 10 million ha remain to be harvested, in Siberia and the Russian Far East.
Farmers are striving to bring in crops before permanent cold weather and snow sets in.
